transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-26
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CISO, Pegasus), Samir Patel (Head of Platform), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Tom Reed (Legal, joined 15:45)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Pegasus is evaluating Redwood for text-generation/chat/embedding workloads. Main gating items: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration and RBAC model, audit logging and retention, KMS/encryption options (bring-your-own-key), data residency and retention windows. They are leaning towards Dedicated for predictable latency but want Private for certain regulated datasets. Action: share certs and questionnaire, schedule follow-up deep-dive and pilot.

Topics:
- Compliance (SOC2, ISO)
- Identity & Access (SSO/SAML, RBAC)
- Cryptography (KMS/BYOK, HSM)
- Audit & Logging (retention, exportability)
- Hosting modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Data retention and deletion guarantees

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, um i'll hand over to Diego who's the solutions engineer to cover architecture after quick intro.
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: hi thanks, lena here, CISO at Pegasus. we've got Samir and Aisha with me. Tom from legal will jump in a bit. main reason for the call is we need to understand security posture and whether we can use hosted vs dedicated vs private for different data classes.
[00:18] Diego Alvarez: thanks lena. quick overview: Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted API with per-token billing, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed control plane. Today we'll focus on controls: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS.
[00:31] Samir Patel: quick clarification — when you say private, do you mean totally air-gapped or VPC-peered? we have some data that must not leave our cloud region.
[00:38] Diego Alvarez: good q. private can be VPC peered with our control plane or full on-prem where control plane runs in your network. for regulated PII we typically recommend private; VPC peering keeps traffic in-region, and we support customer KMS for key material.
[00:48] Aisha Khan: do you support BYOK into AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault? our secops wants HSM-backed keys.
[00:55] Maya Chen: yes both AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault are supported, and we have a BYOK flow. small caveat: for hosted, redwood holds the control plane but you can provide key policy to restrict access — for private you fully control keys.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: we need to see SOC2 report and ISO 27001 evidence — do you publish those?
[01:15] Maya Chen: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; we also have ISO 27001 certification summary. i'll attach redacted artifacts to the follow-up email.
[01:22] Samir Patel: retention — we have a 7-year retention policy for audit logs and 90-day retention for customer data; can we configure log retention and export?
[01:31] Diego Alvarez: audit logs are configurable in console, you can export to your S3 or SIEM via secure delivery. retention windows can be set — hosted has default retention (90 days for request logs) but on Dedicated/Private you can extend to match your policy.
[01:42] Lena Ortiz: important: we require immutable audit trails for certain actions — separation of duties and an append-only pattern. how do your logs satisfy that?
[01:50] Diego Alvarez: logs are written to an append-only store and we support CDC to your S3 with object-lock if you need immutability. also we support syslog/ SIEM forwarding and rbac alerts.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: for SSO, we use Okta — SAML v2.0. can we do SCIM provisioning and role sync?
[02:12] Maya Chen: yes okta SAML + SCIM is supported, you can map groups to RBAC roles. we have auth flows for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated.
[02:20] Samir Patel: what's the most fine-grained RBAC you support? can we control per-model / per-route permissions?
[02:26] Diego Alvarez: current RBAC is role and token based — you can scope API keys to routes/models/environments. For Private we can enable more granular resource tags to gate model access. we also support token-level audit.
[02:39] Lena Ortiz: wondering about key rotation and key escrow — if we do BYOK, can you rotate keys without service interruption?
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: yes we support rotation with double-wrap pattern; for critical data we recommend Dedicated or Private and a scheduled rotation window, and our rotator supports zero-downtime key roll.
[02:56] Tom Reed: (joined) sorry i'm late — quick Q from legal: do you provide contract language for data deletion and cert of destruction?
[03:02] Maya Chen: yes we provide standard DSR and deletion clauses; for Private you control deletion. we'll share a deletion playbook and certificate template.
[03:12] Lena Ortiz: encryption at rest and in transit — are both covered? any ciphers or minimum TLS versions?
[03:18] Diego Alvarez: TLS 1.2+ strongly preferred; we support TLS 1.3. At-rest encryption is AES-256. For hosted we manage keys unless you provide BYOK.
[03:28] Samir Patel: latency / perf question: some inference paths are latency-sensitive for customer-facing features (50-80 ms). can Dedicated meet that SLA?
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated is designed for predictable latency; we have profiles showing p95 under load. we'll share benchmarks relevant to your model family. Hosted is fast for general use but Dedicated is safer for guaranteed SLO.
[03:47] Aisha Khan: let's talk about data flow for logs — do you redact inputs automatically or do we need to mask client-side?
[03:53] Maya Chen: we do not automatically redact by default; you can apply input filtering via our SDK or use request-side preprocessing. additionally, for Dedicated/Private you can configure automatic masking rules in the console.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: regulatory iso questions: we are also in EU and have data residency constraints. do you have regions and EU-hosted Private options?
[04:12] Diego Alvarez: yes EU regions available, and Private deployments can be provisioned in EU-only regions. for some customers we provision dedicated control plane in-region.
[04:20] Samir Patel: about backups — how long are backups kept and are they encrypted with the same KMS?
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: backups are encrypted with the same key ring, can be stored in your vault for Private. Retention is configurable but default snapshots are 30 days; we can extend per contract.
[04:36] Aisha Khan: compliance scans — do you share vulnerability scans and penetration testing results?
[04:41] Maya Chen: we share summary results and high-level PT reports under NDA; for deeper diligence we can coordinate with security team and schedule a SOC review call.
[04:51] Lena Ortiz: our process requires a network diagram and a list of inbound/outbound ports for firewall whitelisting. can you provide that?
[04:58] Diego Alvarez: yes we'll provide a prescriptive network diagram for VPC peering and private installs — egress endpoints, ports and cert fingerprints.
[05:06] Samir Patel: what about model artifacts: do you cache model weights in the cloud? where do model shards live?
[05:12] Diego Alvarez: good nitty-gritty — models are stored in our artifact store; for Private, artifacts are inside your network, and for Dedicated we can provide options to pin model versions to a storage bucket you control.
[05:24] Aisha Khan: do you have a formal data deletion API for prompt history and KV cache eviction?
[05:29] Diego Alvarez: yes deletion API exists; for Hosted we delete histories per your retention schedule, and you can call immediate purge endpoints. KV caches are ephemeral but can be invalidated on demand.
[05:41] Lena Ortiz: about SSO and SAML assertions — do you log the assertion payloads? any PII in logs?
[05:48] Diego Alvarez: we redact sensitive fields in auth logs by default; you can choose to capture full payloads in a Private deployment if your audit needs it, though we recommend minimal capture.
[05:59] Tom Reed: legal question — breach notification windows?
[06:02] Maya Chen: standard 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate tighter SLAs.
[06:09] Samir Patel: curious about multi-tenancy isolation on Hosted — noise from other tenants is a concern; what isolation mechanisms do you have?
[06:16] Diego Alvarez: compute isolation uses container sandboxes and per-tenant memory separation; we also have model-level quotas and can throttle noisy neighbors. Dedicated gives stronger isolation since capacity is reserved.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: do you perform background model fine-tuning on our data, or is training strictly customer-initiated?
[06:34] Maya Chen: we do not fine-tune on customer data without explicit consent; all training pipelines are opt-in and there are contractual controls.
[06:42] Aisha Khan: do you provide support for logging keys/rotations in our KMS audit trail? we need to see who rotated what.
[06:49] Diego Alvarez: yes the KMS audit trail is visible in your KMS logs; we can correlate actions in our audit logs to KMS events for forensics.
[06:59] Samir Patel: regarding the security questionnaire, is there a canonical spreadsheet that you prefer?
[07:03] Maya Chen: we can accept either your vendor questionnaire or use our quick intake form. preferably send your CSV and we'll map answers quickly.
[07:11] Lena Ortiz: okay, so immediate asks: SOC2 report; ISO summary; SAML/SCIM integration guide; network diagram; deletion playbook.
[07:19] Maya Chen: noted — i'll attach all those. Diego will draft the network diagram template.
[07:24] Tom Reed: one more legal note — export controls and data sovereignty clauses, we'll send language.
[07:28] Maya Chen: thanks, noted — we'll review.
[07:33] Samir Patel: on the hosting decision, we expect baseline usage of 10k req/day but spikes to 100k for seasonal loads. how does autoscaling behave for Dedicated?
[07:41] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies with reserved headroom and burst capacity; we'll propose an autoscale config that matches your traffic profile.
[07:49] Aisha Khan: about billing — do you offer commitments for Dedicated and flexible burst?
[07:53] Maya Chen: yes reserved capacity contracts plus burst credits are supported. pricing details we'll share in follow-up.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: regarding retention/forensics: we might need 7 years of tamper-evident logs. can you commit to storage format compatibility with our long-term archive?
[08:06] Diego Alvarez: yes we can export in standard formats (NDJSON, Parquet) and push to S3 with object-lock for long-term WORM retention.
[08:15] Maya Chen: quick note on evaluations — for your high-risk datasets we recommend Private pilot; for lower-risk features start with Dedicated. we can stage a hybrid approach.
[08:27] Samir Patel: sounds sensible. what's the typical timeline to spin up a Private environment?
[08:32] Diego Alvarez: VPC-peered private can be provisioned in 2-3 weeks once network approvals are done; on-prem full install takes longer (4-8 weeks) depending on ops window.
[08:40] Aisha Khan: any dependencies for on-prem installs? like kernel versions or containers?
[08:44] Diego Alvarez: we'll send an ops checklist — kernel, docker/runtime versions, GPU drivers, NTP configs, and minimum bandwidth.
[08:52] Lena Ortiz: and pen test cadence — do you have yearly third-party pen tests?
[08:56] Maya Chen: yes annual third-party pentests and quarterly internal scans; we provide summary reports to customers under NDA.
[09:03] Tom Reed: do you have SOC2 scope details — which trust services categories are covered?
[09:08] Maya Chen: SOC2 Type II covers security and availability; we can provide scope details in the report.
[09:14] Samir Patel: we also have an internal ops checklist around model governance, can Redwood integrate with our model registry to prevent unapproved models?
[09:21] Diego Alvarez: we have model pinning and version controls; integration via webhook/API is possible to block unapproved artifacts.
[09:29] Aisha Khan: thoughts on data residency controls for EU data — do you offer region-only control plane?
[09:34] Diego Alvarez: we can provision control plane in EU region for your tenant; we'll confirm endpoints and support local KMS.
[09:42] Lena Ortiz: ok last set of clarifying q's: export of raw prompts for QA — do you allow programmatic export?
[09:48] Maya Chen: yes with RBAC gating; exports can be scheduled and purged.
[09:53] Samir Patel: any known limitations about model quantization or artifacts that affect determinism for regen?
[09:58] Diego Alvarez: quantization can slightly change outputs; we recommend testing for regen with your eval prompts. Redwood Optimize has suggestions for quant profiles.
[10:07] Lena Ortiz: great. i think we have enough to move to next step. please include security contacts for direct follow up.
[10:12] Maya Chen: will do. thanks all.
